sec: Vasopressin receptors, actions and countercurrent mechanism

items.q: Match the vasopressin receptor subtype to its intracellular secondary messenger pathway — 1) V1 and V3 receptors 2) V2 receptor … A) IP3 / DAG pathway B) cAMP pathway
items.exp: V1 and V3 signal via IP3/DAG; V2 signals via adenylyl cyclase-cAMP. (Book p960)

items.q: Match the V1 receptor site to its corresponding physiological action — 1) Blood vessels 2) Liver 3) Heart 4) Platelet … A) Vasoconstriction B) Glycogenolysis C) Hypertrophy D) Aggregation
items.exp: V1 mediates vasoconstriction in vessels, glycogenolysis in liver, hypertrophy in heart, and aggregation in platelets. (Book p960)

items.q: Which vasopressin receptor located on anterior pituitary corticotrophs stimulates ACTH release?
items.exp: V3 (V1b) receptors in the anterior pituitary stimulate ACTH release. (Book p960)

items.q: A 19-year-old male with mild von Willebrand disease is administered desmopressin (DDAVP) prior to dental extraction. Desmopressin acts on which endothelial receptor to stimulate vWF release?
items.exp: V2 receptors on vascular endothelium stimulate the release of von Willebrand factor (vWF). (Book p960)

items.q: In the renal counter-current multiplier system, water reabsorption in the descending limb of Henle increases luminal tubular fluid osmolality by:
items.exp: Water reabsorption along the descending limb increases tubular fluid osmolality by 4 times (from 300 up to 1200 mOsm/kg). (Book p960)

items.q: In the renal tubular counter-current system, fluid reabsorption along the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is strictly ___-osmotic.
items.exp: PCT fluid reabsorption is iso-osmotic at approximately 300 mOsm/kg. (Book p960)

items.q: Assess the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle (THAL): I THAL actively reabsorbs solutes (Na+ and Cl-) while remaining impermeable to water. II THAL delivers hypertonic fluid with osmolality exceeding 800 mOsm/kg into the distal tubule.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: THAL reabsorbs solute without water, diluting the fluid to 100-200 mOsm/kg before it reaches the DCT. (Book p960)

items.q: Which component is NOT recognized as maintaining the medullary counter-current exchange mechanism?
opts: Active potassium secretion by intercalated cells
Medullary interstitial osmolality maintained by urea
Urea concentration gradient maintained by vasa recta
items.exp: Counter-current exchange is maintained by medullary interstitium, urea gradient, and the vasa recta; ADH acts only when interstitial osmolality is maintained. (Book p960)

items.q: Match the nephron segment to its role in urine concentration — 1) Descending loop of Henle 2) Thick ascending loop of Henle (THAL) 3) Cortical collecting duct (under ADH) … A) Counter-current multiplier reabsorbing water and raising osmolality 4-fold B) Active solute (Na+/Cl-) reabsorption creating a diluting segment C) ADH-mediated water reabsorption producing concentrated urine (800–900 mOsm/kg)
items.exp: Descending limb multiplies osmolality 4-fold; THAL reabsorbs solutes; collecting duct concentrates urine under ADH to 800-900 mOsm/kg. (Book p960)

items.q: Medullary interstitial hypertonicity is preserved by urea recycling, which is maintained by the hairpin capillary loops of the ___.
items.exp: The vasa recta maintain the medullary urea gradient and interstitial osmolality. (Book p960)

items.q: Under maximal ADH stimulation, the collecting duct concentrates tubular urine to an osmolality of:
items.exp: ADH action in the collecting duct concentrates urine to 800-900 mOsm/kg. (Book p960)

items.q: Under what condition does ADH effectively produce antidiuresis in the collecting ducts?
opts: When the hypertonic medullary interstitial osmolality is maintained
When glomerular filtration rate is reduced by 50%
When aldosterone secretion is completely suppressed
When tubular sodium reabsorption in the PCT is inhibited
items.exp: ADH acts to concentrate urine only when the medullary interstitial osmolality is maintained. (Book p960)
